newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ring cut owners in on car thefts - police.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ring cut owners in on car thefts - police.

text.p: New Jersey police broke up a ring that stole cars with the owners' permission, who not only collected on their insurance but got part of the profit when the cars were sold, officials said Friday.
The gang was nabbed after state police went undercover and pretended they wanted to buy the stolen cars to break up for parts, state Attorney General Peter Verniero said.
The ring operated by getting permission from people to steal their cars, officials said.
The so-called victims would report the thefts to their auto insurance companies and also share in the money the thieves made by selling the cars for parts, they said.
Ronald Cavigliano, of Hillsborough, New Jersey, a salesman for a North Brunswick, New Jersey, auto dealer, allegedly masterminded the operation.
Sixteen other people were arrested on various charges, including insurance fraud, conspiracy, theft by deception, purchase of stolen goods and alteration of motor vehicle records.
Insurance companies paid out about $117,000 because of the scam, officials said.
